event_name: Weaving Demo: The Wild Wild Weft
blurb:
The name alone deserves some credit. The Wild Wild Weft is a two-hour weaving demonstration that runs Saturday afternoon, and it's the kind of hands-on, craft-focused event that tends to be way more interesting in person than it sounds on paper.

If you've got kids who are curious about making things, or you're into fiber arts, or you just want something genuinely different from your usual Saturday afternoon, this fills a gap. It's free, it's indoors, and it's a good option to slot between the morning car show and the evening Halloween events without burning out before the main event.
scoring_notes: Lower mass appeal but high uniqueness score. Arts and crafts demos skew toward families with curious kids and creative adults. Fits the educated demographic profile (50% bachelor's degree or higher). Low stakes, low cost, and fills the afternoon gap on Saturday. Included to give variety in the lineup rather than stacking four near-identical event types.

event_name: Acoustic Jam Session
blurb:
Friday night, live acoustic music, three hours. If you need more than that to decide, you might be overthinking it.

Acoustic sets are low-key in the best way. No overwhelming volume, no cover charge, no pressure to stay for a full concert arc. You can grab dinner nearby, drift in when it's already going, and just let the weekend start the right way. This is a solid option for couples looking for something easy or a small group that wants to actually be able to have a conversation while there's music playing.

Kick the weekend off right. It's free and it starts at 6.
scoring_notes: Recurring events are generally lower priority, but this fills a Friday night adult slot that no other candidate covers. The audience skews 36 median age with dual-income households who want low-effort, low-cost weeknight options. Works for the Flower Mound and Highland Village crowd looking for something easy after the work week. Included because Friday coverage matters and this is the only Friday candidate.

event_name: The Rocky Horror Picture Show Film Screening
blurb:
Look, if you've never seen Rocky Horror in a room full of people who actually know what to do during a screening, you're missing something. This is not a movie you watch quietly. People dress up, shout callbacks at the screen, and generally commit in a way that makes a regular Saturday night at home feel embarrassing by comparison.

Halloween week is the only time of year this one really makes sense, and it's happening Saturday night. The college-adjacent crowd near UNT and TWU will feel right at home here. But honestly anyone who enjoys a little chaos with their cult classics should show up in costume and see what happens.

It starts at 8:00 PM. Come ready to participate.
scoring_notes: Seasonal uniqueness is high since Rocky Horror screenings are essentially a Halloween-only tradition. Strong fit for the younger, college-adjacent segment of the audience and adults who want something that isn't a kids event. Lower family match but that's fine since Little Monsters on Main covers that lane. Good balance in the lineup.

event_name: EsDeeKid at Coca-Cola Roxy
blurb: EsDeeKid hits the Coca-Cola Roxy this Saturday night for a show that runs through 11:30pm. The Roxy is one of the better mid-size venues in Atlanta and it's right at The Battery, so you've got a full night if you want it: dinner before, show, and a place to land after without ever moving your car twice. This is a solid Saturday-night-out option for the crowd that wants live music without a stadium production. Doors open at 7, so get there early if you want to actually be in the room for the start.
scoring_notes: The Roxy is close to the Perimeter coverage area and The Battery is a familiar destination for this demographic. EsDeeKid is a niche pick that may not land with the full audience, but the venue and Saturday timing are strong. Included because it's the only music concert this weekend within reasonable distance.

event_name: Amp It Up Live Music Festival featuring Heart of Atlanta
blurb: Heart of Atlanta, Atlanta's top Heart tribute band, headlines a full outdoor music festival in Roswell this Saturday. The event pulls in local musicians and bands throughout the afternoon and doubles as a fundraiser for Perfect Harmony Health's music therapy scholarship program, which helps individuals with disabilities access music therapy regardless of what they can afford. So you get a great afternoon of live music and the money goes somewhere real. If you've never heard Heart played live by people who actually take it seriously, this is your chance. Roswell Junction is a good outdoor space and October weather is about as good as it gets for this kind of thing.
scoring_notes: Broad appeal, charitable angle adds depth, outdoor festival format works for families and adults alike. Heart tribute band skews slightly older which fits the 38-median-age crowd. Not the highest uniqueness but the cause component gives it more weight than a generic music festival.

event_name: Travel Abroad with the Tritone Orchestras: A Musical World Tour
blurb: The Sunday after Halloween can go one of two ways. This is the good version. Tritone Orchestras is putting on a two-hour world music tour at the Roswell Cultural Arts Center on November 1st, working through genres and musical traditions from across multiple continents in one afternoon. It's a family-friendly option that doesn't feel like you're dragging anyone anywhere, because the concept is genuinely interesting. Music from 20-something countries in a single sit-down performance is not a normal Sunday afternoon, and the Roswell Cultural Arts Center is one of the better venues in the area for this kind of thing. Grab tickets and make the day worthwhile.
scoring_notes: Family-friendly but adult-appealing, fits the mix of young families and empty nesters in the Perimeter audience. November 1st (post-Halloween Sunday) is a good slot with low competition. The world tour concept is more interesting than a standard orchestra performance, which lifts the uniqueness score.

event_name: Lumiere Lounge Jazz Talks with Trey Wright
venue: Earl and Rachel Smith Strand Theatre, Marietta
blurb: KSU Professor Trey Wright is doing something genuinely interesting at the Strand Theatre in Marietta on November 5th. It's not a concert. It's a jazz talk, 30 people max, one drink ticket included, doors at 7pm with the presentation at 7:30. This edition is on Charlie Christian and the evolution of jazz guitar, which is one of those corners of music history that feels obscure until someone walks you through it and suddenly you can't believe you didn't know it sooner. Thirty seats. Adults only (21+). The kind of Thursday night that's worth rescheduling dinner for.
scoring_notes: High education level in this audience makes a professor-led jazz history talk a genuinely good fit. 30-seat cap creates real scarcity. Adult-only format matches the more adult-skewing Perimeter audience. Thursday publish window means this lands with enough lead time to act on it.

event_name: Blacksmithing Skulls with Michael Dillon
blurb: You're going to forge an iron skull. That's the thing. Local artist Michael Dillon, known for large-scale architectural metalwork, is teaching a hands-on blacksmithing session at Art Center West in Roswell this Saturday. You'll work with raw iron, use real tools, and walk out with something you actually made with your hands. It's Halloween-adjacent in the best possible way, and it's the kind of Saturday afternoon that zero percent of your coworkers will have had. Seats are limited by the nature of the space, so if this sounds like your kind of afternoon, don't sit on it.
scoring_notes: High uniqueness score, skilled-instructor-led experience, Halloween timing with the skull theme. Fits the educated, experience-seeking demographic well. Lower demographic fit than bar crawl or dinner party because it's niche, but that niche is strong and the audience can afford it.

event_name: Emo Night and Halloween Party
blurb: If you spent any part of your teens or early twenties listening to My Chemical Romance or Fall Out Boy with the lights off, this one's going to hit. Rock 'N' Taco in Roswell is throwing a Halloween-themed emo night on October 29th with live throwback performances from Pop Rocks ATL. It's early enough in the week that it's not competing with Halloween Saturday, which means the crowd will be smaller and the vibe will be better. Show up in costume or don't, but either way come ready to sing every word to songs you thought you'd forgotten. Starts at 8pm.
scoring_notes: Median age of 38 puts a big chunk of this audience squarely in the emo-era nostalgia zone (early 2000s). Adult-skewing, low barrier to entry, social and fun without being a massive production. The Halloween angle adds seasonal relevance.

event_name: Roswell Boos & Booze Halloween Bar Crawl
blurb: Halloween falls on a Saturday this year, which means the bar crawl situation in Roswell is going to be loud, costumed, and worth showing up for. The 3rd Annual Boos & Booze crawl runs from 3pm to 10pm through Canton Street and the surrounding spots, so you get a full evening without being locked into one venue all night. This is the kind of event that's better with a group. Round up whoever you've been meaning to make plans with, commit to a group costume, and make a night of it. Seven hours of downtown Roswell on Halloween is hard to beat.
scoring_notes: Halloween on a Saturday is a once-every-few-years occurrence that elevates what would otherwise be a recurring event. Adult-skewing, social, fits the young professional and young-family-without-kids-tonight crowd well. Roswell is close enough to Perimeter to be worth the drive for this one.

event_name: "It's Showtime!" A Beetlejuice Dinner Party
venue: Mise en Place Cooking Studio, Roswell
blurb: Halloween is five days away and this one is genuinely different. Mise en Place Cooking Studio in Roswell is throwing a hands-on dinner party inspired by Beetlejuice, and you're not just eating the food, you're making it. The whole thing is interactive, themed from start to finish, and runs just 2.5 hours so it's a real weeknight option without blowing up your Thursday morning. For a $105K household audience that's done the standard haunted house circuit about a dozen times, a cooking class where the menu is the costume is a breath of weird, fresh air. It sells out fast. Don't wait on it.
scoring_notes: High uniqueness, adult-skewing, fits the educated professional crowd that wants experiences over passive entertainment. Halloween timing is perfect for the newsletter window. Cooking studio events tend to sell limited seats, which adds genuine urgency.

event_name: Karaoke Night at Punch Bowl Social
price: Free arcade card with first drink purchase
blurb: If you're looking for something low-commitment and genuinely fun on Friday night, Punch Bowl Social's Karaoke Night is a solid option. The format is simple: live karaoke hosted by Luke Smart's Karaoke, a free arcade card with your first drink, and a crowd that's actually there to have a good time. Punch Bowl Social is already a destination for people who want more than just a bar, and combining the karaoke with arcade games means you're not just standing around waiting for your song to come up. Late start at 9:00 PM puts this squarely in the adults-only going-out category. It's in Atlanta proper, so factor in the drive, but if you've got a group that wants a proper night out before Halloween weekend fully kicks in, this delivers.
scoring_notes: Lowest-ranked inclusion. Karaoke nights are recurring and not particularly unique. However, Punch Bowl Social as a venue has broad appeal for East Cobb's adult audience who go into the city for entertainment. Included as an eighth option because the other seven candidates are stronger, but this serves as a solid out-of-neighborhood option for those who want a livelier Friday. Late start time (9 PM) filters for a younger-leaning adult crowd.

event_name: Coming Out! at Onyx Theatre
blurb: In its fourteenth year, Coming Out! is a performance at KSU's Onyx Theatre that brings together stories, musical acts, and live performance from KSU students and metro-area community members. It's celebratory, thought-provoking, and built around personal storytelling, which makes it feel entirely different from a standard theatrical production. If you've got a college-age kid at KSU, or if live performance that's grounded in real experience is your thing, this is worth checking out. The organizers note it contains mature content, so it's best suited for adults and older teens. Kennesaw is right in the East Cobb orbit, and at fourteen years running this is a well-established event with a real following. Check Onyx Theatre for ticketing details.
scoring_notes: Lower demographic fit because the subject matter may not resonate with the full East Cobb audience, but the KSU connection is meaningful for families with college-age kids (which fits the audience profile well). Fourteen-year run gives it credibility. Mature content flag is appropriate to include. Uniqueness score reflects that it's an annual event, not one-time, but the specific storytelling format and KSU tie-in keep it relevant.

event_name: The Battery Atlanta Movie Series: Sing Sing
blurb: Free outdoor movie at The Battery on a Friday night in October is a hard thing to say no to. The Battery Atlanta Movie Series is showing "Sing Sing" on the Plaza Green this week, which follows Buster Moon putting on a singing competition to save his theater. It's rated G and runs right in line with what you'd want for a relaxed, low-key family evening. The Battery itself means you've got food, drinks, and the whole plaza atmosphere built right in. Pre-purchase a family meal through their site so you're not scrambling when you get there. Bring a blanket, get there before 7:00 PM to claim your spot on the green, and settle in. No tickets, no cover, no stress. Just a movie outside on a cool October night.
scoring_notes: Free outdoor movie is a recurring series (lower uniqueness score) but the specific date, specific film, and Battery Atlanta setting make it a solid inclusion. Fits families with younger or teen kids. High-income audience won't be drawn purely by the free admission, but the experience and convenience of The Battery as a destination give it real appeal. Slightly lower scores because it's a recurring series, not a one-night-only.

event_name: Wildwood Special Screening at Springs Cinema & Taphouse
blurb: Springs Cinema is one of those places that makes a regular movie feel like an actual event, and this one already has something going for it before you even sit down. Wildwood is a handcrafted fantasy adventure with Peyton Elizabeth Lee, Jacob Tremblay, and Carey Mulligan, following a girl on a mission to rescue her baby brother from a forbidden forest. The animation is described as handcrafted, which means this is not your standard CGI blockbuster. It's the kind of film that holds up on a real screen. Two showtimes give you flexibility: 4:30 PM works if you want to make it a late afternoon thing before dinner, and 7:00 PM turns it into a proper Friday night out. Sandy Springs is a quick shot from East Cobb. If you've got kids who are still in that sweet spot for adventure films, or if you just want something visually interesting with a real cast, this is worth the drive.
scoring_notes: Springs Cinema & Taphouse is a known destination for East Cobb residents. Special screening designation suggests this isn't just a standard theatrical run. Family-friendly fantasy with a strong cast fits the mix of established families East Cobb skews toward. Slightly lower uniqueness because it's a movie screening, but the handcrafted animation angle and Springs Cinema's taphouse setting lift it above a generic multiplex night.

event_name: MHS Drama: Blood Wedding
blurb: If you've got a kid in the Marietta school system, or if you just appreciate live theater, this one is worth your Friday night. Marietta High School Drama is putting up "Blood Wedding" by Federico García Lorca, a one-act play about forbidden love, family rivalry, and the kind of choices that spiral out of control. Lorca is legitimate, celebrated literature, not just a school play in the forgettable sense. Seeing a full production of his work done by a strong high school drama program at a real performing arts center is actually a good night of theater. It runs on October 22 and 23, so Friday is your last chance. The Marietta Performing Arts Center is close, the ticket price is going to be modest, and the experience punches above its weight. Go support the kids and see something worth talking about.
scoring_notes: Strong fit for East Cobb families with teens, especially those connected to Marietta-area schools. Established families and empty nesters who follow local arts will recognize the value of Lorca. Two-night run makes it slightly less unique (not a one-night-only), but it closes on Friday October 23 which creates urgency. Local venue, community connection, and the literary credibility of Lorca lift this above a generic school play.

event_name: Halloween Hikes at Chattahoochee Nature Center
blurb: Halloween Hikes at the Chattahoochee Nature Center is one of those events that works for almost everyone in East Cobb. It runs from 7:00 to 11:00 PM on Friday night, which means the teens in your house have something worth doing that isn't sitting on their phones, and the adults can actually enjoy it too. The nature center setting makes this feel different from a typical Halloween event. You're out in the dark, on the trails, with real atmosphere that no haunted house can fully replicate. It's family-friendly but still delivers on the spooky. If you've got kids in the 10-to-17 range who are too old for trick-or-treating but still want to do something for Halloween week, this is the move. Check the Chattahoochee Nature Center website for tickets and details.
scoring_notes: East Cobb audience skews toward families with teens and older kids, and this hits that window perfectly. Roswell location is local and convenient. Evening hours (7–11 PM) make it feel more grown-up than a daytime kids event. Nature center setting differentiates it from generic Halloween fare. Good uniqueness since it's a specific annual event tied to a specific venue with a specific date.

event_name: 5 Wines to Know for Holiday Entertaining
venue: Mise en Place Cooking Studio, Roswell
blurb: With the holidays about six weeks out, this is the kind of prep that actually pays off. A Level One Sommelier named Christina Ruiz is leading a guided tasting of five wines every holiday host should have in rotation: a welcome wine, a crowd pleaser, a charcuterie pairing, a dinner party red, and a cozy nightcap. Each one comes with a bite of food chosen to show how the pairing changes the whole experience. You'll leave knowing what to actually buy instead of just grabbing whatever looks good at Total Wine and hoping for the best. No wine background required, just show up ready to drink and take notes. This is a SMART way to spend a Friday night in October. Grab your spot at Mise en Place before it fills up.
scoring_notes: Strong fit for East Cobb's high-income, educated adult audience who entertain regularly and appreciate a practical, well-run experience. Holiday entertaining framing is timely. Roswell location is local. 21+ adult event fits the empty nester and established family skew well. Uniqueness is slightly lower since cooking studio events recur, but the specific holiday wine angle and timing are relevant enough to include.

event_name: Haunted Spirits at the Southern Museum
blurb: This one is right in the neighborhood and it's not your typical Halloween thing. Haunted Spirits takes over the Southern Museum in Kennesaw for one night, and they've built out a full evening around it. Show up at 6:00 PM to catch a 1938 Hitchcock film in their theater ("The Lady Vanishes," for the film nerds). Then at 8:30 and 9:15, ghost tours of the museum itself get rolling. The whole thing is set up with drinks from Reformation Brewery, cocktails with a costume contest thrown in, and food from 1885 Grill. It's 21+, which tells you everything about the vibe they're going for. This is a genuinely fun adult Halloween night that doesn't require driving into the city or fighting Midtown traffic. Costumes are encouraged, and the costume contest means there's an actual reason to go all out. Grab your tickets on Eventbrite before they're gone.
scoring_notes: Perfect fit for East Cobb's established families and empty nesters who want a polished, adult Halloween experience close to home. 21+ keeps it crowd-appropriate for the 42-median-age audience. Local venue (Southern Museum), local brewery (Reformation), one-night event with multiple programming layers makes it genuinely can't-miss. Price point via Eventbrite is a non-issue for a $118K HHI audience.

event_name: Dueling Pianos at Park Bench
blurb:
No cover. No setlist. Just two pianists going at it for three hours while the crowd decides what gets played. Dueling Pianos at Park Bench in The Battery is the kind of Saturday night that starts as 'we'll just stay for one drink' and ends at midnight.

The show runs 8:30 to 11:30pm. General seating is first-come, first-served and it fills up, so if you're going with a group, reserving a table ahead of time is the smarter move. The Battery makes it easy to grab dinner somewhere first and walk over.

Free admission, good energy, and a crowd that's actually there to have fun. Hard to argue with that on a Saturday night in October.
scoring_notes: No-cover Saturday night entertainment at The Battery is very accessible for this demographic. Interactive format skews adult and social, fits young professionals well. Lower uniqueness score because Dueling Pianos is a recurring Saturday event, not a one-off. Still included because the entertainment value and zero cost are strong selling points for this audience.

event_name: Fair Oaksween 2026
blurb:
Fair Oaks Recreation Center is going all-in on Halloween Wednesday night with music, games, treats, hot cocoa, and costumes. It runs 6 to 8 PM, it's free, and it's built for the whole family.

If you've got kids who want one more Halloween event before the real thing hits Thursday, this is a clean, easy option. Costumes are highly encouraged, which is really the only rule worth following here.

Nothing complicated about this one. Show up in costume, grab some cocoa, let the kids run around. Sometimes that's exactly what the week calls for.
scoring_notes: Lower uniqueness since it's a fairly standard rec-center Halloween party. Skews toward younger families, which is a portion but not the dominant segment of this audience. Included because it's free, local, and falls squarely in the issue window. Good filler pick if the newsletter needs a family-friendly community event.

event_name: Sewell Mill Spook-Tacular
blurb:
Right in the neighborhood and right before Halloween, the Sewell Mill Library is throwing a free costume party Wednesday evening and it's one of the easier wins of the week for families with younger kids still at home.

Costumes are encouraged, activities are family-friendly, and it runs from 5 to 7 PM — early enough to be home and not blow up anyone's school night. Sewell Mill is literally in East Cobb, so you're not driving anywhere. Just show up.

If your kids are the age where Halloween is still a full production, this is a solid warm-up to the main event Thursday night.
scoring_notes: Strong geographic fit — Sewell Mill Library is directly in East Cobb. Skews toward families with younger kids, which is a subset of this audience. Free and low-effort to attend. Uniqueness is lower since it's a fairly standard library Halloween event, but the proximity and timing lift it for this newsletter.

event_name: Halloween Cocktail Class at ASW Distillery
blurb:
ASW Distillery is running a Halloween cocktail class Sunday afternoon, and if you've ever wanted to actually learn what you're doing behind a bar instead of just guessing, this is a fun way to spend a few hours.

You get your own bar station, a lead mixologist walking you through the process, and three cocktails made from award-winning spirits to show for it. Halloween theme gives it a little extra energy. It's at the Battery, so you're looking at a 30-ish minute drive from East Cobb, but the afternoon timing makes it an easy out-and-back.

Good date option. Good friend-group option. Three cocktails and new skills by 5 PM is a pretty solid Sunday.
scoring_notes: Hands-on experience events play well with East Cobb's educated, higher-income adult audience. Halloween theming adds seasonal relevance. The Battery location is a slight friction point for East Cobb residents but not a dealbreaker at $118K median income. Skews adult, which fits the empty nester segment well.

event_name: Fifth Annual WE CARE Veterans Fair
blurb:
If you or someone in your family has served, this one is worth putting on the calendar for Thursday. The WE CARE Veterans Fair is a free benefits expo at the Cobb County Civic Center, running all day from 9 AM to 6 PM.

It's built for veterans, active-duty members, National Guard and Reserve, military families, caregivers, and survivors — basically anyone connected to service who wants to know what benefits and resources are actually available to them. East Cobb has a meaningful veteran population, and a lot of people leave benefits on the table simply because they don't know they exist.

This is the fifth year running, which means it's an established event with real resources behind it. Free, local, and genuinely useful. Pass this one along to anyone in your circle who served.
scoring_notes: Annual event rather than a one-night-only, which limits uniqueness. But the civic relevance is high and East Cobb's homeowning, established-family demographic likely includes veterans or military families who would benefit. Free, daytime, and local makes it low-friction to attend. Worth including for community service value.

event_name: Grand Opening: Emily Bourne Grigsby and Athos Menaboni Gallery
blurb:
Kennesaw State is opening a brand new gallery Saturday afternoon, and grand openings are one of those things that only happen once. The Emily Bourne Grigsby and Athos Menaboni Gallery joins KSU's Arts District, and this is your first shot to walk through it before it becomes a regular stop.

Athos Menaboni was a celebrated Georgia artist known for his precise, luminous paintings of birds and nature — his work ended up in the Smithsonian and the White House. Getting a dedicated gallery space near where a lot of you live is genuinely worth noting. Free to attend, no ticket required, and it wraps up in time to make dinner plans.

If you've got a teenager interested in art or a Sunday-afternoon-museum type in the house, bring them along. This is the kind of local thing that's easy to skip and then wish you hadn't.
scoring_notes: Grand openings are by definition one-time events, which lifts the uniqueness score. East Cobb's educated audience skews toward arts appreciation. Menaboni's Georgia legacy gives it local resonance. Free admission removes any friction. Skews toward adults and culture-minded families.

event_name: Murder Mystery Co. Dinner Theater Show
blurb:
Dinner and a show, except you're also a suspect. The Murder Mystery Co. is back at The Hudson Grille in Kennesaw for a Halloween-season whodunit, and if you've never done one of these, this is the right time of year to try it.

You get a three-course meal, a cast of characters who may or may not be the killer, and a room full of strangers who are all trying to crack the case before you do. It's interactive, it's loud, and it's the kind of night that gets genuinely funny once people loosen up. Great for a date night, a group of friends, or honestly any occasion where you want a reason to talk to people you don't know.

Call the box office at 888-659-2952 to book direct and save $9 in fees. Show runs 6:30 to 9:00 PM, which means you're home at a reasonable hour.
scoring_notes: Good adult date-night or group option, close to East Cobb. The Murder Mystery Co. runs monthly events so it's not truly rare, but the Halloween timing adds some seasonal urgency. Dinner included improves the value perception for a $118K median income audience. Skews adult, which works for this newsletter's mix.

event_name: American Patchwork Quartet
blurb:
Multi-Grammy Award-winning guitarist Clay Ross is bringing the American Patchwork Quartet to the Roswell Cultural Arts Center Friday night, and this one is worth clearing your calendar for.

The ensemble pulls from American folk, jazz, country, West African, and East Asian traditions and weaves them into something that genuinely doesn't sound like anything else. Their debut album landed a Grammy nomination. That's not marketing copy — that's a peer vote from the music industry saying this is the real deal.

It's part of Roswell's American Mosaic Series, which means the programming is thoughtful and the crowd tends to be too. A short drive from East Cobb, good music, and the kind of night out that actually gives you something to talk about afterward. Check Roswell365.com for show times and tickets.
scoring_notes: Strong fit for East Cobb's educated, higher-income, 42-median-age audience. This crowd appreciates live music with cultural depth. Grammy-nominated act elevates the uniqueness score. Proximity to East Cobb makes it a natural pick. Skews adult, which works well for the empty nester portion of the audience.

event_name: Victorian Funeral Flashlight Tour
blurb:
This is not your standard haunted house. The William Root House is going full Victorian death-ritual mode for one night, and honestly, it's one of the more fascinating things happening in Cobb County this Halloween season.

After hours, the rooms go dark and fill up with 19th century embalming equipment, mourning jewelry made from actual human hair, a real death mask, and other artifacts from an era when grief was elaborate, public, and deeply ritualized. You tour it yourself, flashlight in hand, at whatever pace you want. It's eerie without being a jump-scare cheap shot.

If you've got a teenager who thinks Halloween is over once the candy runs out, bring them. If you and your partner are looking for something genuinely different to do on a Friday night, this is it. Arrive no later than 8:30 PM to make sure you get the full experience.
scoring_notes: One-night Halloween event with real historical substance. Skews toward curious adults and older teens, which fits East Cobb's mix of empty nesters and families with teen kids well. Uniqueness is high — Victorian mourning artifacts in a darkened historic house is genuinely rare. Price point is unknown but likely accessible given the venue.
